newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tyumen Oil Co Russian pre-tax falls.
newsitem.headline: Tyumen Oil Co Russian pre-tax falls.

text.p: Preliminary results based on Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis.
Tyumen Oil Company (TNK) is a holding company whose main production unit is AO Nizhnevartovskneftegaz, located in Siberia.
Shareholders will vote whether to confirm results at the annual meeting on Jue 20.
TNK's press service said company management had worked out measures to reduce the fall in production by 22 percent in 1997.
It said the company also planned to increase deliveries to Ryazan oil refinery by 1.8 percent and sales of oil products by 40 percent while reducing its labour force by 5.8 percent.
TNK's production fell to 21.30 million tonnes in 1996 from 22.57 tonnes in 1995.
The Russian government holds 99.98 percent of TNK's shares, while 0.02 percent was sold at an auction at the end of 1995 at which the face value of the shares fell from 1000 roubles to five roubles.

NOTE -- These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
